title: Conormal intersection identity for an ideal quotient generated by a regular sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq J$ ideals of $R$. Assume that there are elements $f_1,\dots,f_c\in J$, with $c\ge0$, whose images $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$ form a regular sequence in $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and generate the ideal $J/I$ of $R/I$. Then $I\cap J^2=IJ$ as ideals of $R$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07CX (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular-ideal), lines 8234-8243, specialized to a regular sequence using Lemma Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular), lines 7265-7298, and Tag 0CEM (lemma-koszul-regular-H1-regular), lines 7300-7308. The proof of 07CX invokes Lemma Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular), whose proof invokes Tag 0665 (lemma-H1-regular-in-quotient), lines 7471-7520. Tags verified in tags/tags.

proof.text: Put $G=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. The generation hypothesis gives $J=I+G$. Distributing ideal products gives $J^2=I^2+IG+G^2$. In particular, each $x\in I\cap J^2$ can be written $x=a+b+y$ with $a\in I^2$, $b\in IG$, and $y\in G^2$; since $a,b\in I$, the element $y=x-a-b$ also lies in $I\cap G$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular), lines 7506-7516: expansion of an element of $I\cap J^2$ after $J=I+G$

proof.text: The images of the $f_i$ are a regular sequence in $R/I$, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-quotient-ideal-intersection] gives $I\cap G=IG$. Apply this to $y$ from step 1. Since $I\subseteq J$ and $G\subseteq J$, we have $a\in I^2\subseteq IJ$ and $b,y\in IG\subseteq IJ$; hence $x=a+b+y\in IJ$. Conversely, $IJ\subseteq I$ and $IJ\subseteq J^2$ because $I\subseteq J$. Thus $I\cap J^2=IJ$. For $c=0$, $G=0$ and $J=I$, so the equality reduces to $I\cap I^2=I^2$.
